scientific_question: Which frozen R47J operator actually discharges transient width-5 clauses back to persisted width 4 on the two nonterminal reset steps: R33 simplification, RUP vivification/restart, affine recognition, or a mixed sequence?
required_measurements: width and CLV before each R47J round
width and CLV immediately after R33
width and CLV immediately after RUP
hash and count of width-5 clauses before/after each operator
first operator that makes max width <=4 on each nonterminal reset step
R33 application count and RUP history count per round
exact final formula hash/CLV/terminal equality against frozen r47j.normalize_to_certified_fixpoint

classification_rule.R33_DOMINANT_WIDTH5_DISCHARGE: Both sealed nonterminal reset steps first cross from width>4 to width<=4 immediately after R33.
classification_rule.RUP_DOMINANT_WIDTH5_DISCHARGE: Both sealed nonterminal reset steps first cross from width>4 to width<=4 immediately after RUP.
classification_rule.MIXED_R33_RUP_WIDTH5_DISCHARGE: The two reset steps use different first width-discharge operators, or a step requires multiple operator rounds before crossing.
classification_rule.AFFINE_OR_TERMINAL_PREEMPTION: A nonterminal sealed reset step is no longer a nonterminal reset because affine/semantic terminal preempts width discharge; this is treated as scientific drift unless frozen R47J agrees exactly.

success_ceiling.purpose: Identify the smallest existing proof-carrying operator responsible for the observed representation reset, so the next theorem/counterexample gate targets that exact mechanism.
